items_missed: No 'How are you today?' — went straight from name confirmation into move details
No agenda statement — 'if you had some time to discuss your move for just a little bit' does not tell the customer what will be covered or how long it takes
Never offered packing services, even though the customer said outright 'I don't have any moving boxes' and was calling her case manager about it
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
No 'pricing is super simple' opener and no what's-included list (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools) — only 'we do wrap and pad everything'
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — no insurance content anywhere in the call
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned, even though she opened by walking through the 12:30-2:30 arrival window
Never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and no 'does that make sense?' sense-check after the pricing block

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no prep-shortens-the-move framing, no consolidation examples, no carload tip — despite the customer volunteering that she's purging a balcony and downsizing 2BR to 1BR
Gave a flat 4hr15min estimate with no typical time range for the home size, and never explained what would move that number (stairs, walk distance)
No confirmation email explained — only the Meet Your Mover email and a courtesy call; no bolded-details list, no 'reply with any corrections'
No hours or direct contact info given, just 'reach back out to us'
No Ecobox referral despite the customer actively hunting for boxes
Used the customer's name maybe twice (and got it wrong both times — 'Aaron', then 'Al' for Aryn); leaned on 'ma'am' instead
top_strength: Handled the drawers-and-trash-bags question honestly instead of dodging it — told her unsealed drawers wouldn't be moved, then immediately gave her a usable benchmark ('for a one bedroom we usually see about fifteen to 25 boxes') so she left with a concrete next step. Also caught and noted the $500 SAFE Austin voucher and confirmed it essentially covers the 2.5-hour minimum.
coaching_note: This customer handed her the Save Your Ass speech on a plate — no boxes, a balcony full of purge items, downsizing to a smaller unit — and it never came. Run the prep speech (prep shortens the move and lowers the bill, consolidate loose items, take a carload) on every confirmation call, and pair it with an Ecobox referral when the customer says they have no boxes.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and reassuring through a distracted customer (kids and a dog in the background) with real warmth markers like 'no worries' and 'we can definitely do that for you' — the customer closed with 'you've been wonderful' — though the heavy 'Mm-hmm' filler and mispronounced name keep it short of Outstanding.
